﴿Have you not seen﴾ is an interrogative of wonder (*istifham ta'ajjub*), meaning: be amazed. ﴿How your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ *Rabbuka* (your Lord) refers to *Mahmud*, and its companions are Abraha, the king of Yemen, and his army. He built a church in Sana'a to divert the pilgrims away from Makkah. A man from Kinanah defiled it and smeared its qibla with excrement to show contempt for it. Abraha swore that he would surely demolish the Ka'bah. He came to Makkah with his army, mounted on elephants from Yemen, at the head of which was Mahmud. When they set out to demolish the Ka'bah, Allah sent against them what He related in His saying:
﴿Has He not made﴾, i.e., He made ﴿their plot﴾ in demolishing the Ka'bah ﴿go astray﴾, meaning a loss and destruction.

﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks﴾, groups upon groups. It is said that it has no singular, like أَسَاطِير (asatir, "legends"). It is also said that its singular is أُبُول, أَوْ إِبَال, or إِبِّيل, following the patterns of عُجُول, مِفْتَاح, and سِكِّين.
﴿They pelted them with stones of baked clay﴾ — clay that has been fired.

﴿So He made them like eaten straw﴾, like the leaves of a field of crops that animals have eaten, trampled and destroyed. That is, Allah the Exalted destroyed them, each one by a stone on which his name was written. It was larger than a lentil and smaller than a chickpea, and it would pierce an egg, a man and an elephant and reach the ground. This was the year of the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ).
